sandeep: Quick thought: can we accept writes locally for lower latency but ensure final residence in tenants home region via an escrow + forwarder? Curious about policy modes and operator implications.

aj: I like the latency win. Main risk is copies leaving region even briefly. Need clear tenancy policy mapping.
maria: From compliances POV we must classify tenants as: STRICT (no data may leave), ESCROWABLE (may be temporarily queued but never exported), and OPEN. That changes allowed implementation drastically.
tim: Implementation idea: local accept -> write to local ephemeral escrow store (encrypted, tenant-scoped) -> enqueue forward job id. Forwarder pools are tagged by region; only resident-region pools can dequeue ESCROWABLE/STRICT jobs.
sandeep: Sequence sketch: client -> edge proxy -> local-store+escrow write -> return 202 + escrow_id -> forwarder reads escrow -> resident-store commit -> ack -> local mark committed -> emit audit event. If forward fails, escalate to operator queue.
aj: What should proxy return? 200 vs 202 vs 409? For STRICT we should reject (409 or 425). For ESCROWABLE return 202 to indicate async commit. OPEN can be 200 for backwards compatibility.
maria: Agree. Also legal: escrow storage must be encrypted with keys that are region-bound (KMS regional keys); ephemeral caches must not replicate outside region. Need audit trail with where each piece lived and who accessed it.
ops-bot: Telemetry requirements: counter: queued_escrow_items_total{tenant_residency}, gauge: escrow_queue_depth{region,tenant_residency}, hist: forward_latency_ms_p50_p95. Alerts: escrow_queue_depth(region=eu)>5000 OR forward_latency_p95>5s.

aj: We'll add header propagation: X-Tenant-Residence and X-Escrow-ID. Forwarder must verify header and only run if running in matching region (verify via local region tag).
tim: Conflict model: keep simple LWW with version token plus operator-driven manual reconciliation if divergent; log both versions. CRDTs are attractive but scope creep.
sandeep: Open questions for RFC follow-up: 1) exact retry/backoff for forwarder (retry budget vs dead-letter), 2) escrow retention policy and SLO, 3) encryption key scoping, 4) client-visible semantics (202 vs 200), 5) operator tools for replay/abort.
maria: I'll draft legal matrix mapping country-specific constraints -> allowed residency enum. Also need instructions for on-prem/private deployments where region constraints differ.
aj: I'll prototype a proxy shim: check tenant residency, write to escrow (S3-like bucket with region tags), emit X-Escrow-ID, return 202 for ESCROWABLE. Pushing branch feature/escrow-forwarder-probe.

sandeep: Assignments: @aj prototype, @tim design forwarder retry/reconciliation, @maria legal gating and audit requirements. Weekly sync Friday 11am to review PoC.

ops-bot: Meeting created: "Escrow forwarding PoC review" Fri 11:00.

aj: Note: telemetry will redact escrow ids in logs and strip in public metrics.
maria: Please cc legal on the PoC repo and include a small threat model for regional disclosure.
sandeep: Thanks everyone. We'll fold RFC action items into follow-up doc with concrete API semantics. :white_check_mark:
